title: Ramanujar’s Journey to Sri Rangam
body:
Ramanujar’s Journey to Sri Rangam

After the miracle performed by Swami Ramanujar at the king's court, he gained an unbelievable amount of fame among the masses. This caused Yadava Prakashar’s jealousy to stir up even further. This caused Swami Ramanujar’s mother to get worried. She told Swami Ramanujar that his guru was not showing the ideal characteristics of a teacher as he was getting jealous of his students’ achievements, and that Swami Ramanujar should withdraw from Yadava Prakashar’s gurukulam. 


Thus, Swami Ramanujar stopped attending his lessons at the gurukulam. At this same time, Aalavandaar, who was residing in Sri Rangam, wished to see Swami Ramanujar so that he could take him under his wing as a disciple. To make this a certainty, Periyanambi, who was one of Aalavandaar's foremost disciples, was sent to receive Swami Ramanujar from Kanchipuram. Thus, Periyanambi rushed to Kanchipuram and found Swami Ramanujar performing kainkaryam to Sri Varadaraja Perumal in the form of getting water from a well for the Lord. Periyanambi went to Swami Ramanujar and told him the wish of his Acharya, who wished to take Swami Ramanujar under his tutelage. 


Swami Ramanujar was elated by the news and chose to travel to Sri Rangam to become Aalavandaar's disciple. Upon reaching Sri Rangam, sad news reaches the ears of Swami Ramanujar, saying Aalavandaar had attained Paramapadam. According to Guru Parampara, we cannot treat Paramapadam here as death but as a state of coma, the reason for which we will discuss further. 


When Swami Ramanujar went to see Aalavandaar's mortal remains, he noticed that Aalavandaar's right hand was holding up three fingers. When Swami Ramanujar asked the fellow disciples why he was holding out three fingers, they said those three fingers represent Aalavandaar's final wishes that he wished Swami Ramanujar to carry out. The three requests are as follows:
1) To write a commentary on the Vedanta Sutras that were written by Maharishi Vedavyasa, revealing its knowledge to the commoner.
2) To honor Maharishi Vedavyasa, who wrote the Mahabharata, and Maharishi Parashara, who wrote the Vishnu Puranam, by naming two capable people after their names.
3) To propagate the Visishta Advaita Philosophy, name a person after Nammazhwar and get them to write a commentary for the Tiruvaimozhi.


As Swami Ramanujar vowed to satisfy each of these three wishes, Aalavandaar's three fingers closed into his palm, and a sense of satisfaction was visible on his face. Thus, we can infer that Aalavandaar was in a state of coma and had not yet attained Paramapadam. After Swami Ramanujar took these three vows, Aalavandaar truly attained Paramapadam.
